name: LM13700MX_NOPB
title: LM13700 dual operational transconductance amplifier with linearizing diodes and buffers
summary: Two independent current-controlled transconductance amplifiers in one 16-pin package, each with differential inputs, a push-pull current output whose transconductance is set by the bias current IABC over 6 decades, a pair of input linearizing diodes and a Darlington output buffer. The channels share only the supplies and are well matched. Uses include voltage-controlled amplifiers and stereo volume controls, filters, oscillators, resistors and multipliers, multiplexers, timers and sample-and-hold circuits. LM13700MX/NOPB is the SOIC-16 on a 2500-piece reel.
key_figures: 9600 µS typ (6700 to 13000) at IABC = 500 µA
500 µA typ at IABC = 500 µA, RL = 0
36 VDC or ±18 V max; ±4.75 V to ±16 V or 9.5 V to 32 V single recommended

notes: M is the SOIC-16 in tubes of 48, MX the SOIC-16 on reels of 2500, N the PDIP-16 in tubes of 25.

circuits.title: Voltage-controlled amplifier (typical application)
circuits.description: A volume control on ±15 V. The input reaches the + input through RIN (30 kΩ) and the 1 kΩ divider, whose wiper is grounded, so the amplifier sees a small fraction of the signal between its inputs. A 13 kΩ resistor from +VS feeds about 1 mA into the linearizing diodes. The gain-control voltage drives IABC through 30 kΩ, and the output current develops a voltage across RL (30 kΩ) that the on-chip Darlington buffer delivers, loaded by 5 kΩ to -VS.

parts.note: potentiometer: pins 1 and 2 are the ends, W the wiper; RB lies between pin 1 and the wiper, RA between the wiper and pin 2

notes: Either amplifier of the pair can be used.

circuits.title: Voltage-controlled amplifier
circuits.description: The voltage-controlled amplifier, with the same parts as the typical application. The 1 kΩ potentiometer is trimmed to minimize the control signal's effect at the output.

parts.note: potentiometer: pins 1 and 2 are the ends, W the wiper; RB lies between pin 1 and the wiper, RA between the wiper and pin 2

notes: Either amplifier of the pair can be used.

circuits.title: Stereo volume control
circuits.description: Both amplifiers run as voltage-controlled amplifiers from one control input: VC drives the two IABC pins, tied together, through a single 30 kΩ resistor, so the two channel gains track. Each channel has 10 kΩ input resistance, a 1 kΩ trim potentiometer RP between its inputs with the wiper grounded, 15 kΩ diode bias from +15 V, a 10 kΩ load on the transconductance output, and a 5.1 kΩ buffer load to -15 V.

parts.note: RP, channel 1; potentiometer: pins 1 and 2 are the ends, W the wiper
RP, channel 2; potentiometer: pins 1 and 2 are the ends, W the wiper

notes: RP sets the output offset; in AC-coupled use two 510 Ω resistors can take its place.

circuits.title: Amplitude modulator
circuits.description: A two-quadrant multiplier. The carrier VIN1 enters through 10 kΩ at the inverting input, with a 1 kΩ offset potentiometer (wiper grounded) across the inputs; the modulating signal VIN2 sets IABC through RC (30 kΩ). 15 kΩ from +15 V biases the diodes, RL is 10 kΩ and the buffer is loaded by 5.1 kΩ to -15 V.

parts.note: VOS trim; potentiometer: pins 1 and 2 are the ends, W the wiper

circuits.title: Four-quadrant multiplier
circuits.description: The modulator with RM (10 kΩ) added from VIN1 to the transconductance output. RM injects the current that cancels the constant term of the modulator's output and also acts as the load for IO. RC (50 kΩ, adjustable) from VIN2 sets IABC and is trimmed for VO = 0 V at VIN2 = 0 V. VIN1 reaches the inverting input through 5 kΩ; 10 kΩ from +15 V biases the diodes; the buffer drives 10 kΩ to -15 V.

parts.note: VOS trim; potentiometer: pins 1 and 2 are the ends, W the wiper

circuits.title: AGC amplifier
circuits.description: Gain is controlled through the diode bias current instead of IABC. IABC is fixed by 30 kΩ from +15 V. The input comes in through 250 kΩ, with a 25 kΩ offset potentiometer across the inputs. The output VO feeds a 100 kΩ potentiometer to ground whose wiper drives the Darlington buffer; the buffer charges a 20 µF capacitor through 50 Ω, and that node feeds the diode bias pin. When VO grows to about 3 VBE, enough for the Darlington and the diodes to conduct, the rising ID lowers the gain and holds VO at that level.

parts.note: VOS trim; potentiometer: pins 1 and 2 are the ends, W the wiper
output amplitude; potentiometer: pins 1 and 2 are the ends, W the wiper

circuits.title: Voltage-controlled resistor, single-ended
circuits.description: The terminal VO looks like a resistor to ground whose value is set by VC. The voltage at VO, taken through the buffer, is divided by R (100 kΩ) and RA (200 Ω) onto the inverting input, so the amplifier input stays in its linear range; the resulting output current flows back into VO through the coupling capacitor. The + input returns to ground through 200 Ω; VC sets IABC through 30 kΩ; the buffer is loaded by 10 kΩ to -15 V. RX = (R + RA)/(gm RA).

circuits.title: Voltage-controlled resistor with linearizing diodes
circuits.description: The single-ended voltage-controlled resistor with the diodes in use: 15 kΩ from +15 V supplies ID, and the 1 kΩ potentiometer RP across the inputs (wiper grounded) both trims offset and takes the place of RA in the feedback divider with R (100 kΩ) from the buffer output. The diodes improve the resistor's noise. VC sets IABC through 30 kΩ; the buffer is loaded by 10 kΩ to -15 V.

parts.note: RP, VOS trim; potentiometer: pins 1 and 2 are the ends, W the wiper

circuits.title: Floating voltage-controlled resistor
circuits.description: Both amplifiers make a resistor whose two ends float anywhere within the output range. Each end is an amplifier output, buffered and fed back through R (100 kΩ) to the inputs, which are cross-connected through RA (1 kΩ). One 15 kΩ resistor from VC feeds both IABC pins. Each buffer is loaded by 10 kΩ to -15 V. RX = 2R/(gm RA).

circuits.title: Voltage-controlled low-pass filter
circuits.description: A first-order low-pass whose cut-off follows IABC. The input is attenuated by 100 kΩ and 200 Ω onto the + input; the buffered output returns through R (100 kΩ) and RA (200 Ω) to the inverting input. The transconductance output charges C (150 pF). Below cut-off the circuit is a unity-gain buffer; above it the response falls 6 dB per octave. VC sets IABC through 30 kΩ; the buffer is loaded by 10 kΩ to -15 V.
notes: fo = RA gm / ((R + RA) 2πC).

circuits.title: Voltage-controlled high-pass filter
circuits.description: The low-pass arrangement with the capacitor moved: VIN drives the transconductance output node through C (0.005 µF), giving a single roll-off below a cut-off set by IABC. A 10 kΩ potentiometer between the supplies, through 220 kΩ into the + input (1 kΩ to ground), nulls the offset. R (100 kΩ) and RA (1 kΩ) feed the buffered output back to the inverting input; IABC comes through 30 kΩ; the buffer is loaded by 10 kΩ to -15 V.

parts.note: VOS null; potentiometer: pins 1 and 2 are the ends, W the wiper

notes: fo = RA gm / ((R + RA) 2πC).

circuits.title: Voltage-controlled 2-pole Butterworth low-pass filter
circuits.description: Two low-pass sections in cascade, one per amplifier, both biased from VC through one 15 kΩ resistor. Each section has the 100 kΩ / 200 Ω input attenuator and 100 kΩ / 200 Ω feedback divider. The first section's capacitor C (100 pF) runs from its transconductance output to the final output VO; the second uses 2C (200 pF) to ground. Each buffer is loaded by 10 kΩ to -15 V.
notes: fo = RA gm / ((R + RA) 2πC).

circuits.title: Voltage-controlled state variable filter
circuits.description: Two integrators (each a transconductance stage into 800 pF, buffered) in a loop give band-pass and low-pass outputs whose frequency follows VC, applied to both IABC pins through 15 kΩ. The input arrives through 10 kΩ with 1 kΩ to ground; 20 kΩ resistors return both outputs to the first amplifier's inverting input; 20 kΩ and 1 kΩ pass the band-pass output to the second stage. Buffers are loaded by 5.1 kΩ to -15 V.

circuits.title: Triangular/square-wave VCO
circuits.description: Amplifier 1 is an integrator: IC, set by VC through 30 kΩ, charges or discharges C (200 pF), and its buffer gives the triangle VO1. Amplifier 2 is a comparator with hysteresis: its current IA (from +15 V through 51 kΩ) into RA (5.1 kΩ) sets a square wave that drives both + inputs. Buffers are loaded by 10 kΩ to -15 V. fOSC = IC/(4 C IA RA); with these parts, IC from 1 mA down to 10 nA sweeps the output from 200 kHz to under 2 Hz, and IA × RA sets the amplitudes.
notes: Keep the peak voltage between the inputs under 5 V; beyond that the input junctions zener.

circuits.title: Ramp/pulse VCO
circuits.description: The triangle VCO changed so that charge and discharge rates differ. VC sets IC into amplifier 1's bias through 510 kΩ; while VO2 is high, amplifier 2's buffer adds IF through 30 kΩ and C (50 pF) charges fast; while VO2 is low IF is zero and IC alone discharges C. R1 (100 kΩ) and R2 (24 kΩ) set the comparator threshold VPK. IA comes from +15 V through 51 kΩ; amplifier 1's buffer is loaded by 10 kΩ to -15 V.
notes: VPK = (V+ ± 0.8 V) R2/(R1 + R2); tH ≈ 2 VPK C / IF; tL = 2 VPK C / IC; f0 ≈ IC/(2 VPK C) for IC << IF.

circuits.title: Sinusoidal VCO
circuits.description: Two LM13700 packages: amplifier A1 works as a limiter/inverter and A2, A3 and A4 as voltage-controlled low-pass sections (300 pF each, 100 kΩ / 220 Ω feedback dividers) in a ring. Oscillation occurs where the loop phase reaches 360°: 180° from the inverter and 60° from each filter. VC sets A2's IABC through 30 kΩ and A3's and A4's through 15 kΩ; A1's IABC is fixed by 30 kΩ from +15 V. The range is 5 Hz to 50 kHz with THD under 1 %.
notes: A1 and A2 are U1's amplifiers 1 and 2; A3 and A4 are U2's amplifiers 1 and 2.

circuits.title: Single amplifier VCO
circuits.description: One amplifier and its buffer form a relaxation oscillator, leaving the other amplifier free. C (0.05 µF) couples the transconductance output to the + input, which two antiparallel 1N914 diodes clamp to ground. R1 (10 kΩ) from the buffered output and R2 (2 kΩ) to ground set the inverting input. VC sets IC through 30 kΩ; the buffer is loaded by 5.1 kΩ to -15 V.

circuits.title: Zero stand-by power timer
circuits.description: A one-shot that takes no supply current until triggered. A positive trigger of at least 2 V, through 0.01 µF and 1 kΩ, lifts the output node; RB (10 kΩ) from there feeds IABC, turning the amplifier on, and 10 kΩ pulls the + input (3 kΩ to ground) high. The amplifier latches high while C (1 µF) charges through 20 kΩ towards the + input level; then the output falls, the amplifier switches off and C discharges. With the diode bias pin joined to the inverting input, C also discharges through the diode DI. The pulse is about 7 ms. V- is grounded.
notes: The other amplifier, biased from VO, can do another job and likewise draws nothing on stand-by.

circuits.title: Multiplexer
circuits.description: An MM74C74 flip-flop clocked by CLOCK steers bias current through 12 kΩ from Q or Q̄ to one amplifier at a time. Both amplifiers are unity-gain followers sharing one output: the transconductance outputs are joined, and both buffer outputs and both inverting inputs are tied to VO (10 kΩ to -12 V). The biased amplifier forces VO to its own input. CC (150 pF) and RC (300 Ω) stabilize the followers. Slewing into 150 pF caps the clock near 200 kHz when VIN1 and VIN2 differ by the largest allowed 5 V.
notes: U2 pins are named by function: GND (to ground), CLK, Q, QN (Q̄) and VNEG (to -12 V).

circuits.title: Phase lock loop
circuits.description: Amplifier 1 is the four-quadrant multiplier used as phase detector and amplifier 2 the single-amplifier VCO. VIN enters the multiplier through two 10 kΩ resistors (one to the inverting input, which has 10 kΩ to ground, one to the output node); 1.0 µF filters the multiplier output, whose buffer, loaded by 3 kΩ to -15 V, steers the VCO's bias through 30 kΩ. The VCO output VO (3 kΩ to -15 V) returns to the multiplier's IABC through 30 kΩ. The VCO uses 0.033 µF, two 1N914 clamps, 1.5 kΩ and 10 kΩ. Centre frequency 1 kHz, hold-in ±5 %, input sensitivity about 300 mV.

circuits.title: Schmitt trigger
circuits.description: A comparator whose hysteresis is the amplifier's output current IB flowing in R (10 kΩ), the resistor from the + input and output node to ground: VH = 2 × R × IB, about 2 V with 82 kΩ from +5 V setting IB. Changing IB changes the hysteresis. VIN drives the inverting input; the buffer output VO is loaded by 10 kΩ to -5 V.

circuits.title: Tachometer
circuits.description: A frequency-to-voltage converter. Amplifier 1 squares up the input (0 to 1 kHz) with IB from 33 kΩ. Each positive edge pushes a charge (VH - VL) Ct through Ct (0.01 µF) into amplifier 2's bias pin, and amplifier 2 delivers it into Cf (10 µF) and Rt (36 kΩ); the average balances VO/Rt, so VO ≈ 10 mV per Hz. D1 (1N914, anode to -15 V) discharges Ct when amplifier 1 goes low. The highest input frequency is set by the time IB takes to carry Ct between the output's low and high limits, VL and VH.

circuits.title: Peak detector and hold circuit
circuits.description: Amplifier 2 compares VIN with VO and, while VIN is higher, its output current biases amplifier 1, which charges the storage capacitor C (0.33 µF) until VO equals the input peak. A logic level at the control terminal (+15 V detect, -15 V hold) pulls amplifier 2's output low through D1 (1N914), switching amplifier 1 off so VO stays put. VO is the buffered capacitor voltage, loaded by 10 kΩ to -15 V; 30 kΩ from +15 V biases amplifier 2.

circuits.title: Sample-hold circuit
circuits.description: A follower that samples while the control input (+5 V sample, -5 V hold) supplies IB through 10 kΩ and holds when IB stops. VIN drives the + input; VO, the buffer output loaded by 1 kΩ to -5 V, returns to the inverting input. CC (1000 pF) in series with RC (100 Ω) runs from the transconductance output to ground. Supplies ±5 V.

circuits.title: Ramp and hold
circuits.description: Amplifier 1, its bias fixed by 43 kΩ from +15 V, switches on when RAMP ENABLE goes high and its output current IB becomes amplifier 2's bias. Amplifier 2's + input goes to +5 V or -5 V through a switch (ramp up or ramp down), so it sources or sinks IB into C (0.2 µF); with IB gone, C holds. The buffer gives VO, loaded by 1 kΩ to -5 V. The ramp rate is about 1 V/ms with these values.

parts.note: C common, UP to +5 V, DOWN to -5 V

circuits.title: True RMS converter
circuits.description: An AGC loop that holds the AC power at amplifier A1's output constant. A2 (diodes biased by 24 kΩ from +15 V) squares A1's buffered output; A3 (half an LM1458) integrates the result against VREF (100 kΩ from -15 V, 1.3 kΩ to ground) and, through 2 kΩ and PNP Q1 (base held by 1 kΩ / 1.2 kΩ), supplies ID to A1's diodes, attenuating the input. A4 (the other half of the LM1458) balances the diode currents so its output VO is proportional to the input's RMS value; the 1 MΩ calibration resistor is set so VO reads RMS volts directly, about 1 % accurate. A 1 MΩ potentiometer nulls the bias current; 1/gm is trimmed with 5 kΩ in series with 12 kΩ.

parts.note: dual op amp: A3 is half 1, A4 half 2
bias current null; potentiometer: pins 1 and 2 are the ends, W the wiper

notes: U2 pins are named by function: IN1-, IN1+, OUT1 for A3 and IN2-, IN2+, OUT2 for A4; its supply pins are not drawn.

circuits.title: Delta VBE reference
circuits.description: A voltage reference whose temperature coefficient is adjustable. 30 kΩ from +15 V feeds amplifier 1's + input and diode bias pin, joined, so the diode D1 between them and the grounded inverting input conducts; the same node drives amplifier 2's + input directly and its inverting input through 1 kΩ. Amplifier 1's IABC is set by 360 kΩ and amplifier 2's by 180 kΩ, both from +15 V. The joined outputs (0.01 µF to ground) drive buffer 2, whose output VOUT (100 kΩ to -15 V) returns through the 100 kΩ potentiometer to amplifier 2's inverting input. The output is about 1.2 V; the TC is positive above 1.2 V, zero near 1.2 V and negative below.
notes: Amplifier 1 uses pins 2 and 3; amplifier 2 uses pins 13, 14 and 15.

circuits.title: Pulse width modulator
circuits.description: The clock, through 500 pF and 1 kΩ, triggers both amplifiers' + inputs. Amplifier 1 (IABC from 30 kΩ to +15 V, 15 kΩ output load) gives the output pulse at VOUT; while it is high, 10 kΩ holds the + inputs up. Amplifier 2 integrates on 800 pF with a current IC set by the control voltage through 30 kΩ; its buffered output returns through 100 kΩ to amplifier 1's inverting input and ends the pulse, so the width TP follows the control voltage, with TP ≤ T/2.

circuits.title: Logarithmic current source
circuits.description: Produces an IABC that varies exponentially with a control voltage, over 4 to 6 decades. Amplifier 2's + input is held at 0 V by the loop, so amplifier 1's output current equals I3 = -VC/RC; -VC enters through 150 kΩ. Amplifier 1 (I2 set by RC = 100 kΩ from +15 V) sees the difference between the bases of the matched PNP pair Q1/Q2 (2N3726), attenuated by R1 (1 kΩ) and R2 (5 kΩ). Amplifier 2's buffer drives the pair's emitters; Q1, diode-connected, carries I1 set by 15 kΩ to -15 V, and Q2's collector delivers IABC. The output can bias the stereo volume control.
notes: IABC = I1 exp(-C I3 / I2).

circuits.title: Unity gain follower
circuits.description: One amplifier as a voltage follower. The input, terminated in 51 Ω, reaches the + input through 10 kΩ; 390 pF in series with 1.3 kΩ runs from the + input to the inverting input. 10 kΩ in parallel with 0.001 µF feeds the transconductance output back to the inverting input. IABC comes from 62 kΩ to +15 V; both supply pins are bypassed with 0.01 µF; the buffer output is loaded by 5 kΩ to -15 V.
notes: Pins are given in pairs (3,14; 2,15; 4,13; 1,16; 5,12; 7,10; 8,9) so either amplifier serves.

circuits.title: Leakage current test circuit
circuits.description: The leakage measurement: with IABC and the buffer input grounded, the inputs, diode bias pin and output are tied together and connected through an ammeter and a changeover switch either to +36 V or to ground.

parts.note: C common, 1 to +36 V, 2 to ground

circuits.title: Differential input current test circuit
circuits.description: The differential input current measurement: IABC is tied to V- (-15 V) so the amplifier is off, the + input is grounded, and ±4 V is applied to the inverting input through an ammeter.

operation.text: Each channel is a differential pair (Q4, Q5) whose tail current is IABC, mirrored in from the bias pin by Q1, Q2 and D1. Three current mirrors subtract the two collector currents to make the output current, so the output is a current source and gm is proportional to IABC, adjustable over 6 decades. Apart from the buffer transistors Q12 and Q13, every transistor and diode in the channel is the same size. The two channels share only the supplies.

Above a few millivolts of differential input the plain pair turns nonlinear. Two diodes, matched to the input transistors and biased by ID from the diode bias pin, sit across the inputs; driving them with a signal current IS makes the output an exact linear function of IS as long as IS stays below ID/2. Resistors instead of current sources for the bias cause only small errors. With the diodes the amplifier takes larger inputs for the same distortion, about 10 dB better signal-to-noise referred to 0.5 % THD. 1 mA is the suggested ID; a large ID lowers the diodes' dynamic resistance and helps the linearizing.
Each channel has its own Darlington emitter-follower buffer able to deliver up to 20 mA. Its input bias current, and so the DC level of its output, does not depend on IABC (unlike the LM13600).

Single or split supplies work with few changes. On ±5 V the signal range is reduced because the PNP transistors have a larger VBE than the NPNs. The outputs survive being shorted to ground indefinitely.

The example targets a 1 VP input, THD below 0.1 % on ±15 V, a control voltage from −13 V to 15 V and more than 30 dB of gain range. The diode bias pins sit one diode drop (+0.7 V) above the 0 V input level, so a resistor from V+ drops 14.3 V; 13 kΩ gives about the suggested 1 mA, and ID must exceed twice IS. For under 0.1 % THD with diodes the differential input must stay below 60 mVpp; the input divider brings 1 VP to 33 mVpp. The bias pins sit two diode drops above V−, −13.6 V on these supplies, so 1 mA at VC = 15 V needs 28.6 kΩ; 30 kΩ is used, and the gain is linear in the applied voltage.

Signal-to-noise improves with larger IABC and with larger input signals. Set the input level with RIN until distortion is just acceptable, then pick RL for the output swing wanted. The diodes add negligible noise compared with the amplifier's transistors.

The 13 kΩ diode-bias resistor can be modelled as a current source, with the input network as a Thevenin source (RTH = RB); the circuit then behaves like the current-driven linearizing diode arrangement.

Because the buffers are on chip, the amplifier makes voltage-controlled filters directly. In the low-pass, cut-off falls at the frequency where XC/gm reaches R/RA, the loop's closed gain. More amplifiers give higher orders (the 2-pole Butterworth, the state variable filter); because gm tracks well between the two channels they stay accurate across several decades of frequency.

Either a single supply or a dual supply can be used. The supplies should have low impedance and good bypassing with low-ESR ceramic capacitors of adequate voltage rating; on a dual supply the bypass capacitors return to ground.

Mount the supply bypass capacitors right at the supply pins, the smallest value nearest the pin. Use a ground plane and keep signal traces off any gaps in it. Keep feedback parts and passives close to the pins; a capacitor that limits bandwidth goes nearer the pin than any ballast or gain resistor. In the recommended layout each channel's input, bias and buffer parts sit on its own side of the package, with the supply bypass capacitors at pins 6 and 11.
ESD protection is limited; store and handle with the leads shorted or in conductive foam.
